articles.title: Brit Arrested After Flight Attendant Finds Hidden Camera In Airplane Bathroom, Now Faces Voyeurism And Cover-Up Charges - Live and Let's Fly
articles.description: A flight attendant discovered a hidden camera while using the lavatory on a Scoot flight from Japan to Singapore. A British passenger now faces charges of voyeurism and obstructing justice, with police alleging that he remotely activated the camera and later tried to erase evidence after realizing it had been found. Hugh Lutley, a 52-year-old British national, was charged on November 5, 2026, following an incident aboard Scoot flight TR821 from Osaka (KIX) to Singapore (SIN) on October 7. He faces one charge each of voyeurism and obstruction of justice. It appears Lutley intends to plead guilty, was offered bail of S$10,000, and has a pretrial conference scheduled for November 17 (which of course is not a conviction or a sentence). Police Say The Camera Was Activated Remotely The Singapore Police Force's account describes an alleged attempt to record people inside an aircraft toilet. Police say the passenger concealed a camera in the lavatory, left, and activated its recording function through an application on his phone. A cabin crew member subsequently used the lavatory and discovered the device. She removed it and immediately alerted a colleague. The passenger allegedly returned to retrieve the camera, found it missing, and deleted the application and related photographs from his phone in an attempt to avoid detection. Police detained him when the flight arrived at Singapore Changi Airport and seized his phone and the camera. The Alleged Cover-Up Carries A Higher Maximum Penalty Police identify two potential penalties: * Voyeurism * Obstructing justice Those are statutory maximums, but the alleged attempt to destroy evidence exposes him to a charge carrying a substantially longer maximum prison term than the underlying voyeurism charge. A Locked Lavatory Door Should Mean Privacy There is something particularly vile about placing a camera in an aircraft lavatory. Passengers and crew have little choice about where to go, and closing and locking the door should allow them to expect privacy. I am thankful the flight attendant found the device and reported it. Discovering something like that while using the restroom must be deeply unsettling. The published accounts do not establish how many people, if any, were recorded before the camera was discovered...the alleged installation and remote operation are disturbing enough. Is this world so twisted that passengers must become amateur surveillance experts every time they use an airplane bathroom? If you notice an unfamiliar device or something suspicious, alert the crew promptly...yeah, I guess you should look around before you drop your drawers. CONCLUSION A British passenger faces criminal charges after a flight attendant found a hidden camera in a Scoot lavatory. Police allege he remotely operated it and then deleted material from his phone after discovering the camera had been removed. The case remains before the court. For now, credit to the crew member who discovered the device and acted. An tight aircraft lavatory may offer very little comfort, but privacy ought to be a given.

articles.title: British SCOOT Passenger Arrested In Singapore For Installing Spy Camera In Lavatory
articles.description: According to the Straits Times, the offender is now facing severe penalties if convicted, including a prison sentence and caning. A man who allegedly hid a camera in the restroom of a Scoot plane on a flight from Osaka, Japan, to Singapore has been charged with one count each of voyeurism and obstructing the course of justice. On Nov 5, Hugh Lutley, 52, a Briton, appeared in a district court accused of committing the offences on board the budget carrier at or around 5.10pm on Oct 7. In a statement on Nov 4, the police said he allegedly activated the camera's recording function remotely through an app on his mobile phone after leaving the restroom. A cabin crew member, who was using the restroom, found the hidden camera. She removed the device and alerted her colleague. Lutley allegedly tried to retrieve the camera later, but found that it had been removed. He is said to have deleted the app and all related pictures on his phone to avoid detection. He was detained at Changi Airport, and the camera and his phone were seized. Lutley's pre-trial conference will take place on Nov 17. For voyeurism, an offender can be jailed for up to two years, fined, caned, or receive any combination of such punishments. An offender convicted of obstructing the course of justice can be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both. Some os the charges brought forward now include obstruction os justive in addition to the voyeurism counts, likely because of the deletion of the material from his cellphone. Very strange approach since this was done even before he was officially accused of any crime, but whatever, Singapore has an odd legal system, and this guy certainly deserves everything that's coming for him. We have covered a bunch of misconduct by passengers over the years, and some of those included various sex crimes that were either direct assaults or, in this case, voyeurism with the use of electronic devices. I often wonder why and how people get so sick as to plan a deliberate mission to install mobile cameras in an airplane lavatory, connected to a cellphone. Probably some kind of home protection device designed for a totally innocent use within the confines of your home or the front door. Conclusion Singapore has another travel-related criminal case ongoing, as a British citizen was arrested following his flight on Scoot from Osaka to Changi. He is being accused of installing a spy cam in the lavatory of the aircraft that operated his flight. When a flight attendant discovered the device and ripped it off, the alleged offender deleted all material from his cellphone that could have linked him to the crime. Reports do not ascertain how they connected this passenger to the camera or what kind of evidence was used to establish probable cause in this case. Even after deleting the app and videos or pictures, I'd think that it at least requires a forensic analysis of the device to trace and prove the allegations.

pendingReview.description: Content warning: This article contains information about alleged child sexual abuse material. Reader discretion is advised. Report CSAM to law enforcement by contacting the ICAC Tip Line at (801) 281-1211 or your local law enforcement agency. PROVO, Utah (ABC4) -- An Orem man is behind bars after he allegedly recorded an 11-year-old girl while she was in the changing room at Ross. Daniel Donofrio, 36, has been arrested on one count of voyeurism for recording a child under 14 years old, a third-degree felony. According to the arrest statement, the Provo Police Department responded to the Ross Store at 1235 S University Avenue on Nov. 8. When officers arrived, an 11-year-old told them that she was using the changing room when she saw a phone appear over the top of the stall next to her. There were only two changing room stalls, located at the front of the store. A family friend, Donofrio, brought the 11-year-old to the store to try on clothes. Officers retrieved surveillance footage from the store, which reportedly showed Donofrio sitting across from the dressing room. He then stood up and entered the stall adjacent to where the child was, stayed in there for 40 seconds, and returned to the chair. The child's mother identified Donofrio in the video, and he was seen with longer hair and a beard. A warrant was approved for Donofrio's residence and cell phone. Officers brought him in for questioning, but stated that his answers were "inconsistent." He also allegedly changed his appearance by cutting his hair and shaving off his beard. In speaking with police, Donofrio claimed that the victim's mother told him to check the stall and make sure no one is in there. She later stated that she never asked him to do that. The 36-year-old then claimed that he went into the changing room to "walk around," but it was a very small room. Donofrio told officers that the 11-year-old's mother had blocked him, and he deleted all of the photos of their family that he had. The mother alleges that he sent her a picture of him holding a knife next to his arm and made suicide threats after she told him she was going to Ross to get the surveillance footage. Donofrio was arrested and booked into the Utah County Jail, where he is being held with bail.
